records.name: Business and individual volunteer opportunities (Parks and Recreation)
records.summary: The general entry point for weeding, planting, trail clearing, rec center after school help and special event volunteering such as the Broad Street Run, outside of a specific Friends group.
records.what_you_do: Pull weeds, plant, clear trails, or help at a rec center or a special event such as the Broad Street Run.

schedule.text: Second Saturday of each month, starting at 10 am. Each month's workday is in a different park.

requirements.gear: Tools and work gloves are provided at some workdays. Bring your own water.

access.notes: Some parks have no restrooms, and the Cobbs Creek workday page says so.

first_step.how: Register for a Second Saturday workday at loveyourpark.org/volunteer/secondsaturdays, using the sign up link on the event you choose.
first_step.basis: The Second Saturdays page says no experience is needed, all are welcome, and each workday has its own sign up link.
first_step.what_to_expect: A workday starts at 10 am and runs about two hours in a city park. You might plant trees, pull invasive plants, or clean up trash and waterways, and some events supply tools and gloves. Nobody needs experience to join in.
first_visit_tips: Sign up on the event page first, since each month's workday is in a different park.
Bring water, because some parks have no restrooms.
Check the event page before you go, since the Cobbs Creek workday is canceled in heavy rain, thunder, or severe weather.

records.notes: Background clearances: the city page says ongoing positions at a playground or rec center need them. It does not say whether one time or outdoor volunteers need them, so background_check is left out and the clearance line was moved out of what_to_expect. No minimum age or kids policy is stated, so those are left out. Event pages print dates without a year (for example October 10th), so no year is recorded for them. A Fall Weekend mentioned in a home page summary was not confirmed on a readable page, so it is not recorded. The contact email and phone are the PPR stewardship team's, as the city page gives them for parks not on the Friends list. Last sign of life kept from tier 1.

records.name: BYO Printmaking Collaborative
records.summary: A printmaking studio in Old City with equipment for screen printing, etching, relief printing, and book arts. Members share the studio, and the public can visit it on First Fridays.
records.what_you_do: Visit on First Fridays (5 to 8 pm) or book another visit, learn from a member or get a lesson for a fee, or apply for a studio membership.

schedule.text: First Fridays, 5 to 8 pm, open to the public. Other visits by appointment.

cost.text: Studio membership is $125 a month on a one year commitment. Members who book time as needed pay $12 an hour, plus $15 per screen reclaim and exposure. The cost of a First Friday visit is not listed.

first_step.how: Come to a First Friday open studio, 5 to 8 pm, at 12 N 3rd St, #5, and ask a member about making your first print. For a visit at another time, email byostudio.philly@gmail.com.
first_step.basis: The studio says it is happy to teach newcomers, has a Learn with us section for a first print, and opens First Fridays to the public. There is no set beginner class, and membership needs an application.
first_step.what_to_expect: First Fridays run 5 to 8 pm. An October 2026 listing describes the evening as an open studio with collaborative making, so you can see the studio in use and join in with others. Visit costs are not listed, and visits at other times need an appointment.
first_visit_tips: For a visit outside First Fridays, email the studio first, since those visits are by appointment.
Check the calendar page before you go, because the events listed there change.
The studio is in Old City at 12 N 3rd St, #5. The pages do not give parking or transit details.

records.notes: Membership is $125 a month, capped at 25 members, and needs proficiency in a printmaking field. Applications are rolling, and applying puts you on a waitlist when space is short. Intaglio Club sessions ($40 a session, aimed at intaglio printmakers) appear for 2026 but are for experienced printmakers, so they are not a first step. Second Sundays drop in hours ($12 an hour to print) appear only in the 2025 listings. The About page says the studio moved to the Paradigm Arts Building in Old City in 2024. The address on record is 12 N 3rd St, #5, and was not checked against that building. Tier 1 had drop_in and newcomer rating 3; the newcomer rating is now 4 from the studio's own words on newcomers.

records.name: C.O.D.E. (Community of Developers & Engineers)
records.summary: A community for people who build software in Philadelphia. Members meet for weekly coding sessions to work on problems side by side, and the group runs a hackathon every quarter.
records.what_you_do: Bring a laptop, work on your own code or a challenge with others, and help newer members get unstuck. Some weeks focus on practice problems.

schedule.text: Weekly coding sessions, with LeetCode Wednesdays as one regular focus. Times and places are posted on Meetup.

cost.text: No session fee is listed. The group asks for donations and sponsors.

first_step.how: Join the group's Discord and introduce yourself, RSVP for a session on Meetup, and bring a laptop.
first_step.basis: The onboarding page says no experience is needed and lists three steps for new people. It does not describe a formal orientation or buddy program.
first_step.what_to_expect: A session is a work time where members code side by side on their own projects, a course, or a shared challenge such as practice problems. Bring a laptop and something to work on. The page suggests introducing yourself to at least one person, and the group also runs workshops, AI paper discussions, and a quarterly hackathon. Sessions need no application, and the page lists no fee.
first_visit_tips: Introduce yourself in the Discord intro channel before the session, so people know who you are.
Bring a laptop and a project or practice problem you want help with.
Check Meetup for the time and place, since the group does not name a fixed weekly venue.

records.notes: The About page says the group was founded in 2024. The onboarding page asks people to RSVP on Meetup but does not say whether walk-ins are welcome, so drop_in is left out; tier 1 had it as true and the reading did not confirm it. Hackathons were held at Pennovation Works and Cesium in the most recent listing, and are not used as a regular location. The group's own pages name Discord and Meetup as the join routes.

records.name: Cannonball Festival
records.summary: A nonprofit that puts on a yearly festival of circus and performance art in Philadelphia, with an open call for performing artists.
records.what_you_do: See circus and performance shows during the festival, which are listed in the Philly Fringe lineup filtered for Cannonball. Performers can apply through the Artist Open Call, and visitors can donate or join the mailing list.

schedule.text: Held once a year, with shows across about three weeks.

cost.text: Ticket prices are listed on each show's ticket page.

first_step.how: Pick a show from the Audience Paths 2026 list or the Philly Fringe lineup filtered for Cannonball, then buy tickets through that show's own ticket page. If you perform, read the Artist Open Call before you apply.
first_step.basis: Shows are open to the public and sold through Philly Fringe ticket pages, and the audience guide groups picks for first time Fringe goers. Buying a ticket is the only sign up, so the way in is clear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The festival runs in weeks, and its audience guide groups the shows by theme. Expect circus and performance art, and note that some shows are for adults only. The festival pages we read do not print exact dates, prices, or access details, so check each show's ticket page.
first_visit_tips: Read each show's age note before you buy, since one listed show is 21 and over and several have adult themes.
Check times and prices on each show's ticket page, because the festival home and visit pages do not print them.
Each venue has its own access page on the festival site, so check it before you go.

records.notes: The 2026 festival dates, ticket prices and access details are not printed on the pages read; ticket links go to the Philly Fringe site. The menu label Cannonball 2026 has a year but no month, so last_sign_of_life stays empty. The Artist Open Call page prints an April 19 deadline with no year. That date is before today, so the record does not present the call as open. Performer tracks, for reference: Buy-In keeps ticket sales after Fringe fees; Co-Presentation has a $300 refundable deposit; special tracks pay stipends from $500 to $5,000; Work-Trade keeps ticket sales with the artist in exchange for 10 to 20 hours a week of festival volunteering. The vocabulary has no circus tag, so variety_cabaret is the closest fit. Venues named include Asian Arts Initiative and Icebox Project Space; each venue's access page was not read.

records.name: Capitolo Community Garden
records.summary: A community garden in Capitolo Playground at Tenth and Federal Streets, founded in 2009. It has 54 in-ground plots and three raised beds, and members share the garden's upkeep.
records.what_you_do: Members keep a plot, attend two workdays and two meetings each year, and take turns on shared chores such as watering the common beds and taking garden trash to the curb.

schedule.text: Two workdays and two meetings a year for members. The site does not list dates.

cost.text: No plot or membership fee is listed on the site.

access.notes: Three raised beds are set aside for people with limited mobility. The site does not describe paths or wheelchair access.

first_step.how: Email capitologarden@gmail.com or use the Join the Waitlist form on the How to Join page to get on the plot waitlist, and ask when the next common bed workday is.
first_step.basis: Anyone can join the waitlist, and community members are welcome to help with the common beds. The page gives no dates for those workdays, and plots typically wait 3 to 4 years, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Helpers weed, water, and mow the common beds, and members also take turns on shared chores such as moving garden trash to the curb. The garden is organic and focused on sustainability. Children are welcome, and child sized tools are available.
first_visit_tips: Ask by email when the next common bed workday is, since the site does not list dates.
Ask about parking and access before you come, since the site does not describe them.
If you have limited mobility, ask about the three raised beds, which the site sets aside for that.

records.notes: The home page welcomes the new garden members of the 2026 season. That shows the year but no month, so the tier 1 month and source are kept. The footer year (2021) is not evidence. The How to Join page says child sized tools are available but has no formal rules for children, and it says nothing about dogs. No workday or meeting dates are printed. The waitlist is a Google form, and no waitlist fee is mentioned.

records.name: Caribbean Community in Philadelphia
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that puts on Caribbean heritage events, including Caribbean Heritage Day, a film screening and a children's storytime.
records.what_you_do: Come to a public event such as Caribbean Heritage Day, a film screening, or a children's storytime. Watch the CultureWorks community calendar for the next one.

schedule.text: Events are listed on the CultureWorks community calendar, with a cluster in June. No regular schedule is published.

cost.text: Not published in the calendar listing.

first_step.how: Watch the CultureWorks community calendar for the next event listed by Caribbean Community in Philadelphia, and go to it.
first_step.basis: The group's own site could not be reached, and the only way in we can see is a community calendar listing that does not print a place, a price, or whether the event is open to everyone.
first_step.what_to_expect: Events are one-off gatherings such as a heritage day, a film screening, or a children's storytime. The calendar entries we found do not print a place, a price, or an open to everyone note, so check the entry closely before going. Costs are not published.
first_visit_tips: Check the CultureWorks calendar entry for the place and time before you travel.
If the entry does not name a venue, do not assume the event is open to walk-ins.
Plan for a children's program if you are bringing kids, since the storytime listing is aimed at children.

records.notes: The group's own website returned HTTP 404 on both the https and http addresses on 2026-10-08, so no pages from the group were read. Contacts are left as tier 1 had them until the site is checked. The CultureWorks June 2026 listings name this group as presenter of Caribbean Heritage Day (June 6, 2026, 4 pm), a Queer Caribbean Shorts film screening (June 23, 2026, 6 pm), and a children's storytime (June 24, 2026, 1:30 pm). None of those entries prints a location, a cost, or an open to public note. A June 19 watch party and the Philadelphia Caribbean Carnival and Parade are listed under the United Caribbean Association of Philadelphia, a separate group, and are not recorded here. A web search returned older history and a personal contact for this group; those are not the group's own pages, so no facts or personal contact details were recorded from them.

records.name: Casa de Duende
records.summary: Supports under-served artists, especially immigrant, Indigenous and LGBTQI+ artists, through exhibitions, a bilingual English and Spanish press, and performances.
records.what_you_do: Send an enquiry through the contact page or email the artistic director about exhibitions, performances, or the press. Public events such as readings are listed on the current programs page.

schedule.text: Exhibitions, readings, and performances come and go, and are listed on the current programs page. No regular schedule is published.

cost.text: Costs are not listed on the pages we read.

first_step.how: Check the Current and Upcoming Programs page for a public event, such as a reading, or send an enquiry to ask how to attend.
first_step.basis: Public readings say everyone is invited and give a date, time, and venue, but no sign up route is printed. Other routes, such as exhibitions, press, and performances, start with an email enquiry.
first_step.what_to_expect: Events are public readings, exhibitions, and performances, and the press publishes in English and Spanish. The March 2026 anthology reading ran at 5 pm at Samuel S. Fleisher Art Memorial, and the page says everyone is invited. Prices are not printed, so check with the organizers before you go.
first_visit_tips: Confirm the time and place by email before going, since the office lists no visiting hours.
Look for the venue on each event listing, because the office and the events are in different places.
The office is at The Philadelphia Building, 1315 Walnut Street, Suite 300, but ask before you visit.

records.notes: Tier 1 confidence was low. The March 2026 reading on the current programs page raises it to medium. The contact page sends questions through an enquiry form, and no phone number or visiting hours are listed. Dos Lenguas Press publishes bilingual literature in translation, with editors named on its page. No open call or submission route was found. The programs page also lists a 2024 festival event and an October event with no year printed, and neither is used. Fiscal sponsor per tier 1 is CultureWorks.
